plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Sell QQQ and trim QQQI and SMH to exit or reduce positions flagged by the scanner.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a potential target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by cutting leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration, leading to lower expected drawdowns.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 1% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Sell QQQ and trim QQQI to reduce exposure to flagged downtrends.
Buy RGTI at 4% to add a strong risk/reward long setup from the scanner.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets growth with a risk-first approach, aiming for ~2.5% per month. It reduces leverage and concentration while introducing a high-quality new setup, balancing potential returns with controlled risk.

plan: Add to SOXL and SPAL, targeting 6% each, to increase leveraged exposure.
Buy RGTI at 6% to lean into a high-scoring scanner setup.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Sell QQQ and trim QQQI to exit or reduce positions flagged by the scanner.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan aims for stretch growth, targeting ~4% per month, by increasing leveraged ETF exposure and concentrating in high-scoring setups. Be aware this significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk, with leveraged ETFs subject to daily decay and rebalancing.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30%, to increase income-generating exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Sell QQQ and trim SMH to reduce exposure to downtrends and high-beta names.
income.read: This income plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions, targeting ~1% per month, by rotating into income-focused ETFs. While aiming for low drawdown and reliable income, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in market selloffs.
